input.quote: 9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no indemnification clause of any kind: searches for "indemn", "hold harmless", "defend" and "infring" return only incidental references (Section 19.4 "indemnified claims", Section 21.3 "its indemnification obligations", Section 29.2 indemnity notices, Section 30.5 "indemnified party"), and the Section 20 cross-referenced in Section 9.3 ("the remedies required by Section 20.5") does not exist anywhere in the document. With no Vendor IP indemnity at all, the document falls into walk-away territory under this critical rule, and the surrounding provisions are left with broken cross-references. We inserted a new Section 20 at the preferred position (Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; usual exclusions; notice/control/cooperation procedure; procure-modify-replace-refund remedies in 20.5 to match the Section 9.3 cross-reference) with our own indemnity kept narrow to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

proposal.summary: Insert missing Section 20 (Indemnification): Vendor IP/law/data/misconduct indemnity, standard procedure and IP remedies, narrow Customer indemnity.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no indemnity section at all, even though Sections 9.3, 21.3 and 30.5 already assume one (9.3 cross-refers to "the remedies required by Section 20.5"). We have added a standard Section 20 giving us a Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with the usual exclusions, notice/control/cooperation procedure and procure-modify-replace-refund remedies, and a narrow reciprocal indemnity from us limited to our content and our breach of law.

ops.text:
20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
20.2 Section 20.1(a) does not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's unauthorized modification of the Services or a Deliverable, combination of the Services or a Deliverable with items not supplied or recommended by Vendor where the claim would have been avoided absent the combination, or Vendor's compliance with Customer's written specifications.
20.3 Customer shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Vendor from and against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of content Customer provides to the Services in violation of a third party's intellectual property rights, or Customer's breach of Applicable Law. Customer has no other indemnification obligation under this Agreement.
20.4 The indemnified party shall give the indemnifying party prompt written notice of the claim, tender control of its defence and settlement, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense. The indemnifying party may not settle a claim in a way that imposes liability, an admission, or a non-monetary obligation on the indemnified party without its prior written consent. The indemnified party may participate with its own counsel at its own expense, and delayed notice relieves the indemnifying party only to the extent it is materially prejudiced.
20.5 If the Services or a Deliverable are, or in Vendor's reasonable opinion are likely to become, the subject of an infringement claim, Vendor shall at its expense procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected item or modify or replace it with a functionally equivalent non-infringing item. If neither option is commercially reasonable, Customer may terminate the affected Services or Deliverable and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the terminated portion and Fees paid for items Customer can no longer reasonably use.
